newsitem.title: FRANCE: Heads on block in French privatization row.
newsitem.headline: Heads on block in French privatization row.

text.p: The French government asked the head of state insurer GAN to resign Monday after Paris abandoned a tender to privatise GAN's banking subsidiary and criticised the heads of both companies for failing to promote the sale.
"The government has asked for the resignation of Mr. Jean-Jacques Bonnaud," a Finance Ministry spokeswoman said.

Sources said, however, that the government's wrath over the privatisation failure looked set to claim the chairmen of both firms -- Bonnaud and Bernard Yoncourt, chairman of its profitable regional banking subsidiary Credit Industriel et Commercial, known as CIC.
A source close to the case said the new GAN chairman would name a new boss at CIC but declined to give any names.
Neither GAN, Groupe des Assurances Nationales, nor CIC made any immediate comment on the news.
The government made it clear last week when announcing the cancellation of the CIC privatisation that Bonnaud, who is ultimately responsible for CIC as part of the GAN group, was on the firing line.
"The managers of GAN and CIC did not behave in a way to encouarge progress in this process," the Finance Ministry said last week.
